headline: Reviewed fiscal year 2027 first-quarter budget and Cross Street training center plans; approved routine reports and minutes.
summary: The meeting covered the fiscal 2027 first-quarter budget, including staffing and vehicle requests. It also covered plans for the Fire and Police Joint Training Center at 30 Cross Street. The board approved the September 24, 2026 minutes and the September monthly reports, and placed a letter from Terryville's fire chief on file.

decision_titles: Letter from Terryville Fire Chief Mark Sekorski
plain_text:
Board of Fire Commissioners’ Regular Meeting       
October 22, 2026 
 
A Regular Meeting of the Board of Fire Commissioners was held on Thursday, October 22, 
2026, at 6:00 p.m., in City Hall meeting room 3-1, 111 N Main Street, Bristol, CT 
 
 
Present: Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu, Commissioners Dana Jandreau, Hal Kilby, Anthony 
Benvenuto, Sandra Bogdanski, and Dannette Rodriguez, Council Member Peter Kelley, and Fire 
Chief Richard Hart 
 
1. CALL TO ORDER 
a. Mayor Zoppo-Sassu called the meeting to order at 6:00 pm. She led introductions and the 
Pledge of Allegiance.  
 
2. CITIZEN RECOGNITION 
a. Bristol Resident Kristen Labbe was recognized for her outstanding kindness and compassion at 
a motor vehicle accident involving children.  
 
3. EMPLOYEE RECOGNITION 
a. None. 
 
4. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION 
a. None.  
 
5. COMMUNICATIONS 
a. Chief Hart shared a letter from Mark Sekorski, Terryville’s Fire Chief, expressing his 
gratitude and appreciation for assistance with a structure fire on October 7th. 
Commissioner Kilby moved to place the letter on file, and Commissioner Bogdanski 
seconded.  The motion passed unanimously.  
 
6. APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES 
a. Commissioner Kilby moved to approve the September 24, 2026 regular meeting minutes 
with the correction of Commissioner Benvenuto’s last name in the motion for adjournment, 
and Commissioner Bogdanski seconded the motion. The motion passed unanimously.     
 
7. APPROVAL OF THE MONTHLY REPORTS 
a. Commissioner Jandreau moved to accept the September monthly reports, and 
Commissioner Benevenuto seconded. The board unanimously approved the September 
monthly reports and placed them on file. Discussion followed.  
• Commissioner Jandreau raised concern over the limited increase in private hydrants 
that have become compliant. Chief Hart shared that the Fire Marshal will send a
letter through their compliance system to notify anyone who has not serviced their 
hydrants of impending fines if they are not in compliance.  
• Concern was raised over alternative ways people may try to heat their home this 
winter and what Public Service Announcements the department can provide to 
help people safely heat their homes. Mayor Zoppo-Sassu suggested creating a 
brochure with resources to hand out to anyone who may need heating assistance 
while on calls, and to anyone of immediate concern being referred to Community 
Services and/or the Building Department.  
b. Commissioner Benvenuto moved to jump to New Business item 10.a. Fiscal Year 2027 
Quarter 1 Budget Review. Commissioner Jandreau seconded. The motion passed 
unanimously.  
 
8. COMMITTEE REPORTS 
a. Fire Station 3 Building Committee 
• The committee is still open, as some items are still being addressed with the 
contractor. The building warranty expires in mid-March, and the project is 
expected to close after that.  
b. Personnel Committee 
• None.  
9. OLD BUSINESS 
a. Fire and Police Joint Training Center Update 
• Rough plans for the building at 30 Cross Street were presented to the Board 
and reviewed.  
• Chief Hart shared that the Fire Academy sent a member out to the Cross Street 
property and is temporarily looking to move the CPAT Testing indoors. Chief 
Hart and the member discussed exchanging academy tuition for the state’s 
CPAT use of the property. Chief advised that two seats in the February academy 
class will be needed to cover the retirements of Deputy Chief David Butkus and 
Captain Brian D’Amato in July.  
 
10. NEW BUSINESS 
a. The Fiscal Year 2027 Quarter 1 Budget was reviewed.  
• Chief Hart shared that the new Apparatus Mechanic, Brendan Yerger, is getting 
settled in and making repairs that are saving the department greatly on parts 
upcharges and labor. He noted repairs he made to Engine 7 and Tower 1 and 
the significant savings both financially and on apparatus out-of-service time.  
• Chief Hart advised that for the Fiscal Year Budget he will be requesting the 
following items: 
• Permission to hire 16 Firefighters and the ability to apply for the 
SAFER Grant to staff Ladder 2.  
• The addition of an Assistant Chief to assist with the division of labor 
of administrative duties, grant applications, and succession planning.
• Two additional Fire Inspectors. With this, he will review potential 
revenue from plan reviews and applications. Chief Hart hopes to 
make one inspector position a dual role that will handle Fire 
Prevention and Community Relations.  
• A code increase for his Administrative Assistant.  
• Vehicles slated for replacement in this budget cycle are Brush 1, 
Tower 2, Engine 2, and two of the Fire Marshal’s Office vehicles. He 
advised he hopes to repurpose Service 1 as Brush 1 using $41,000.00 
from the Apparatus Replacement account to purchase a utility body 
for Brush, and then use the slated Brush replacement to purchase a 
true Service vehicle for the Apparatus Mechanic. 
• The board discussed the Quarter 1 Budget, noting that Professional Fees has 
been almost completely expended by mandatory annual testing. The Board 
suggested exploring a separate budget line item for these required annual 
tests, which could also improve clarity for the Board of Finance.  
• The department’s Overtime budget usage is at 23% and on target for now, but 
there is concern due to long-term absences and Workers’ Compensation 
delays.   
• The department’s Motor Fuels budget usage is at 23%. Market volatility and 
the current fuel contract expiring in December raise concerns. The Board will 
continue to monitor.  
• The City Department Heads are continuing to work on the Strategic Plan. The 
Board discussed the importance of maintaining concrete data on all items to 
justify increases.  
• The Board discussed that the Town of Southington has rejected the $3.2 
million SAFER Grant that was awarded, which continues to impact their staffing 
and the impacts on Mutual Aid calls to Bristol and surrounding towns. Chief 
Hart advised that he has had many conversations with the Southington Fire 
Chief, Fire Board, Board of Finance, and Town Manager over his support of 
accepting the grant and adequately staffing the town.  
• Mayor Zoppo-Sassu and Council Member Kelley departed the meeting at 6:45 
p.m., and Commissioner Jandreau took over as Chair. Five voting members 
remained present, and a quorum was maintained.  
• Chief Hart reminded the board that the department will be holding Fire 
Operations on Saturday, November 7th. This demonstration will show real-time 
examples of where the department needs additional staffing. Members of the 
Fire Board and Board of Finance have signed up to participate in this training.  
   
 
11. ADJOURN 
a. On motion of Commissioner Rodriguez and seconded by Commissioner Bogdanski, it was 
unanimously voted to adjourn the meeting at 6:58 pm.
Recording Secretary: Sara Bianchi
